quote_text:
If you win the league you do more media. You  happy? Thanks Dave. Richard. Congratulations.  
How are you? Very, very happy, of course,  but to a certain extent also quite unreal  
because you've worked so hard for this moment to  happen. And when it does happen, it needs some  
time for you to truly feel it. But the fans  were so happy that it didn't take us long,  
it didn't take me long to understand what we've  achieved together this season. Chris. Yeah, yeah,  
that is so, so, so special. The moment I knew  I would become the new head coach over here,  
that's already a moment where you're so proud of,  to be part of such a great football club, then now  
to be part of the history of this football club  is something I think I could have only dreamt of  
two, three or four years ago. I don't know if  it's funny or not, but I think it was four,  
five or six years ago. It was the first time when  I was here, when Pep Lijnders invited me, that  
was against Tottenham. I think they won the game  4-0, it was somewhere around Christmas time. And  
we all know what happened around Tottenham one or  two years ago. So now to win it against them is  
quite special. And this week, the one I was  with was my sporting director at Cambuur,  
where I worked back then. He showed me that we  were also visiting a match from the under-21s  
where Joe and Trent were involved in that game.  I don't know where they played, but it was in a  
small stadium. So yeah, special day. And not the  first time I was here when we played Tottenham.  
James. Can you describe what it was like first  arriving at the stadium, seeing the scenes outside  
all the fans, celebrating early really, and then  you know a final whistle when you know that really  
you're on the pitch, what was that like? The only  moment I was emotional today was when we arrived  
at the stadium to see what it meant for the fans,  what it meant for these people. For us to have a  
chance of winning it felt really special, but  immediately it also felt like we still have to  
do it. But I think everybody who was inside that  bus felt if the fans are with us like they are,  
then it's impossible for us to lose this game of  football. So yeah, and then during the game, after  
the game, it's been incredible how the support  of the fans were and how our players played. And  
special, special to be part of this day. Andre?  Arne, how are you celebrating tonight? Probably  
with a glass of beer or two, or maybe three. If  I'm correct, then there will be a little party  
over here with friends, family, so maybe, maybe,  yeah, maybe, maybe not. And so, yeah, the moment I  
leave this room, probably they're going to inform  me what are the plans, but I definitely know it's  
going to be special, but I think there's  one more special moment to come somewhere  
around the twenty-sixth. Yeah, well, what did  John say to you? Probably congratulations. I  
don't remember exactly what he said, but it was  special for them as well, I think, to be part of  
this moment, for them to trust me in this  position. Maybe now everybody says, oh,  
that makes complete sense. But the moment they  signed me, maybe not everyone was as convinced  
as everyone is now. So that tells you also what  a special club this is and that they don't always  
go for the maybe most simple or obvious choice,  but they make the choice that they think is best  
for the club. So it must be a special moment  for them as well, second time in five years,  
that they win the league also. And now to do this  in front of our fans is special for everyone,  
including for them. Luz? And you obviously had  all your family here. How proud does that make  
you your own achievement? Very proud. Very proud,  but it's special to have them with me because my  
family, all of the families of the players have  to make certain sacrifices if you do this job,  
not only this season, throughout your whole  career. Me, like you, everyone works really hard,  
but we're not always home. Of course, for me, my  family was still in Holland, so it was in moments  
hard for me, but definitely for them as well.  And then now to win it, I think then everybody  
feels that all the sacrifices were all, but the  few sacrifices we've made were definitely worth  
it. And then it's special that they can experience  this moment as well. Ollie. It felt like a very  
classy gesture for you to thank when you got on  the microphone. Not a lot of managers would have  
done that, I don't think. Why did you feel the  need to do that? Because of what he did when I  
arrived here, before I even arrived here. I think  that is something not one manager ever did before.  
So that is what definitely helped me. But apart  from that, he helped me even more by the team he  
left behind and the culture we left behind in  that team. The quality the players have was,  
I think, obvious for everyone, but the culture  of hard work, the culture of not only from the  
players but also from the staff members have  been incredible and that is one of the reasons  
why we could achieve what we've achieved  this season. So yeah, for obvious reasons,  
I think it was a nice moment to thank him as well.  Matt. Bill Shankly once said that this win in the  
league is Liverpool Football Club's bread and  butter. Would you agree with that statement?  
He was probably longer in his job than I was. He  knew the club even better than I know it at the  
moment. But what I noticed from the first day  I came in was that winning the league would be  
the most special trophy we could win. And yeah,  I think I felt that throughout the whole season,  
although we were all very disappointed when we  were knocked out by Paris Saint-Germain, but we  
always felt there was a bigger goal to achieve.  And to do that in the most difficult league in  
the world is in a period of time where it gets  harder and harder and harder, probably to win it  
is very special. James. You've been top league  since November. Was there a particular point  
along in that journey when you really start to  believe yourself this as today as possible? Yeah,  
it wasn't today that the first time I felt like  it's possible. I think we felt it is possible for  
quite a long period, but if it's possible, it's  something else, then that you will achieve it. So  
we knew and we still know how hard it is to win  a game of football in this league so that we  
were one of the teams that could win it. I think  that was quite clear from maybe, I don't know,  
maybe from preseason onwards. But then you need  to have consistency and that's difficult, but we  
had that. And that's the reason why we probably  deserved to win it. If you have a margin like  
we have, I think it's fair to say that we deserve  to win this league this season. Last couple here,  
man here. I think you're the first Dutch manager  to win the Premier League title too. How does that  
feel? Special. Because the country I'm from has  a lot of great football players, had a lot of  
great managers as well. Not all of them worked  in England. So then it's also hard to win the  
Premier League if you didn't work here. But to  be the first one is so special because that will  
always be, that will always stay the same. And  especially then to win it at this club. And what  
I mean with that is with the history of the club,  of course, but also if I would have taken over at  
a club that won from the last five seasons, one or  five times in a row, people might maybe say, oh,  
that's not, it's just a difficult job to win and  done. But that's not, although we won it twice in  
five seasons, but it will, City won it, of course,  the last few seasons. So it's special to be the  
number one and it's special to win it over here.  Arne, after such an amazing first season, how do  
you sort of reset expectations for next season?  Now, obviously, how do you sort of build on this?  
Are plans already in place for the summer?  Yeah, definitely. But I don't have to manage  
expectations because the expectations at this club  are always the same. We have to compete for every  
trophy. And that didn't change when I came in and  that doesn't change next season. We have a group  
of players that is able to win things, but we're  not the only one. There are so many great teams  
in this league and in the Champions League,  so it's never going to be easy, but that we  
have to compete. I'm not trying to lower down  the expectations. Next season again, we have  
to compete for every single trophy, and that's  also definitely what we're trying to do. Paul,  
I don't think we are, no. Thank you everyone.  You're welcome. Congratulations. Thank you.
title: CHAMPIONS!  Arne Slot post-match press conference | Liverpool 5-1 Tottenham
